headline: Refugees in Kenya's Kakuma camp say AI is cutting the pay and supply of the low-paid online tech work they rely on.
score_reason: Pool 6; read in full; figures are attributed to the International Trade Centre and to named organisations; no lowering.
importance_line: Refugees and low-paid data workers are losing guaranteed pay and jobs, which affects them first and then the platforms and tech firms that use their work, and the doubt is that the 50 percent drop is one agency's estimate.
summary: The Guardian reports, after interviews with more than two dozen refugees, that low-paid online tech gigs in Kakuma camp are drying up and that some are now paid through 'rewards' rather than wages. The International Trade Centre estimates that jobs such as transcription, data entry, translation and web research have fallen by about 50 percent since 2022, and refugee workers say that as AI speeds up their work, their paid hours and income are falling.
notes: Full text read (fulltext C14-06, Guardian HTTP 200). The Guardian's own reporting, so it is the source. Pool curator note: inequality.
